findings.title: Deleting the cache does not refresh the connectedCalendars query, so the dropdown keeps showing the old state
findings.body:
The only refresh after a cache delete is `onSuccess?.()`, which calls the parent's optional `onChanged`. The disconnect mutation next to it invalidates `connectedCalendars` and `apps.integrations` in `onSettled` (lines 61-64), and the `DisconnectIntegration` it replaces did the same. The delete-cache mutation does not.

`SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` is also rendered from `packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372` without `onChanged`. There the dropdown is still shown, because `hasCache` does not depend on `disableConnectionModification`. After a successful delete the success toast appears, but `cacheUpdatedAt` stays as it was. The "Last updated" row and the "Delete cached data" item remain until the query is refetched by something else.

Fix: invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the delete-cache mutation's `onSuccess` or `onSettled`, as the disconnect mutation does.

findings.title: Handler throws a bare Error, queries Prisma directly, and the input schema lives in the router
findings.body:
1. Line 25 throws `new Error(...)`, which tRPC reports as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. The case is a missing or foreign credential, so it should be a `TRPCError` with NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN.
2. The PR body says the change was reworked to "use repository pattern". The handler still calls `prisma.credential.findFirst` and `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly. `CalendarCacheRepository` has no delete method; the mock does have `deleteManyByCredential`, but the real class does not. A repository method would keep the delete next to `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` and the other cache operations.
3. `_router.tsx:29` defines the input as an inline `z.object`. Sibling procedures in that router use a separate `*.schema.ts` file (for example `ZConnectedCalendarsInputSchema`).

findings.title: New SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump (and the extra selected fields) has no reader
findings.body:
`fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `updateMany({ where: { credentialId } }, data: {})` on every cache refresh, which is every Google webhook. It updates every SelectedCalendar row under the credential, including rows that were not refreshed.

I found no reader of `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. It does not appear in `packages/lib/CalendarManager.ts` or `selectedCalendar.ts`. The UI shows `CalendarCache.updatedAt` through `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`. The `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` additions to `UserRepository` (`user.ts:899-900`) and to `UserWithCalendars` (`getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:23,27`) are unused as well. They only widen the type that `apps/api/v1/pages/api/connected-calendars/_get.ts` must satisfy.

If nothing is meant to consume this, drop the write and the added selects. If something is meant to, name the consumer. `updateMany` with `data: {}` relies on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` bump and is easy to remove by accident.

findings.title: Timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's UI language, while the surrounding label is translated through `t("cache_last_updated")`. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`), or the repo's existing date-formatting helper, so the date format matches the rest of the page.

findings.title: Migration header comment contradicts the SQL
findings.body:
The auto-generated warning (lines 1-6) says the column is added "without a default value". Line 9 adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`. Remove the stale warning so it does not mislead whoever reads the migration later.

Also, existing rows all get the migration time as `updatedAt`. For legacy rows, the dropdown therefore shows the deploy time as "Last updated", not when the cache was actually populated.

findings.title: Dev script: macOS-only sed, success exit code on failure, fragile reuse path, cwd-relative .env
findings.body:
- `sed -i ''` (line 68) is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed it treats `''` as the script and fails.
- `ENV_FILE="../.env"` (line 5) resolves against the caller's cwd, not the script's location. Run from the repo root it writes outside the repository, or creates a new `.env` in the parent directory (lines 62-65).
- `cleanup` always does `exit 0`, so the rate-limit and "Failed to extract URL" paths (lines 49, 58) report success.
- When an existing tmole is reused (lines 28-31), the script reads `/tmp/tmole.log`, which that process may not have written. Reuse then fails with an empty URL. If `pgrep` matches several PIDs, the message prints them all.
- The script is unrelated to the calendar-cache UI. Consider splitting it out, or use `$(dirname "$0")` for the paths and `exit 1` on failure.

findings.title: dev:cron now relies on `npx tsx`, which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: I found no `tsx` entry in any package.json. The repo declares `ts-node` (apps/web/package.json:196, plus the root seed script). `npx tsx` will download an unpinned package on every run, which makes the script non-reproducible. Add `tsx` as a devDependency, or keep `ts-node`. The change is also unrelated to this PR's feature.

contracts.action: Delete cached calendar data for a credential (dropdown item, then confirm dialog, then trpc deleteCache)
contracts.equivalent_path: The disconnect mutation in the same component (trpc.viewer.credentials.delete), and the DisconnectIntegration component it replaced
contracts.before_after: Disconnect invalidates connectedCalendars and apps.integrations in onSettled (lines 61-64) and then calls onSuccess. Delete-cache only calls onSuccess?.() and does not invalidate anything itself.
contracts.visible_effect: Success toast. The timestamp and delete item refresh only if the parent passes onChanged (CalendarListContainer does; the EventAdvancedTab usage does not).
contracts.failure_mode: On error the mutation shows an error toast (line 48) and nothing changes. The dialog is closed before the result arrives. If the server throws, the user sees only the generic toast.

contracts.action: deleteCache handler: remove all CalendarCache rows for a credential
contracts.equivalent_path: handleDeleteCredential for disconnecting (cascade delete of CalendarCache via onDelete: Cascade); the CalendarCache factory CalendarCache.init, which gates on the feature flag
contracts.before_after: Before the delete it re-checks that the credential belongs to ctx.user (`id` and `userId`), which re-verifies the target. The delete is scoped to that single credentialId. It does not go through CalendarCache.init, so the global calendar-cache flag is ignored, which is harmless for a delete.
contracts.visible_effect: Cached free/busy rows are removed. Availability falls back to live Google fetches until the next webhook repopulates the cache. Selected calendars and watches are untouched.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing or foreign credential gives a plain Error, which tRPC reports as 500. The client shows the generic error toast. Nothing is lost on failure.

contracts.action: connectedCalendars handler enriches each calendar with cacheUpdatedAt
contracts.equivalent_path: CalendarCache.init(null), which returns the mock when the flag is off, used in CalendarService.setAvailabilityInCache
contracts.before_after: The handler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly and runs one groupBy query on every connectedCalendars call. CalendarCache.init is not used, so the mock added in this PR is never reached from here. In-memory delegation credentials have negative ids and match no rows, so they get null.
contracts.visible_effect: cacheUpdatedAt reaches the UI as a Date or null, and the dropdown appears for Google Calendar when a timestamp exists.
contracts.failure_mode: If the groupBy throws, the whole connectedCalendars query fails and the settings page breaks, which is a new failure surface for an existing query.

contracts.action: Bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt after every Google cache refresh
contracts.before_after: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache refreshes the cache per eventTypeId group and then, new in this PR, writes to every SelectedCalendar of the credential. No reader of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt was found in this repository.
contracts.failure_mode: An exception in updateMany makes the whole webhook handler fail after the cache was already written.

contracts.action: Added destructive delete confirmation dialogs (delete cache, remove app)
contracts.before_after: Both flows confirm, then call the mutation with the credentialId captured in props. The dropdown is hidden for delegation credentials and when disableConnectionModification is set. The error-state Alert in the wrapper previously ignored disableConnectionModification and now honours it, a small behaviour change.
contracts.failure_mode: A stale credentialId after a list refresh is re-verified server-side. The delete-cache handler checks ownership, and the credential delete goes through handleDeleteCredential.

summary: The calendar-cache dropdown mostly works, with one UI bug to fix in this PR and some cleanups. After a successful cache delete, the dropdown keeps showing the old state unless the parent passes `onChanged`, because the delete mutation doesn't invalidate `connectedCalendars`. The event type tab renders the wrapper without `onChanged`, so it is affected. The new `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` bump on every Google webhook, and the extra selects added for it, have no reader that I could find. The delete handler throws a plain `Error` and calls Prisma directly. Smaller items: a hardcoded `en-US` date format, a stale migration comment, an unrelated dev script that only works on macOS, and `npx tsx` without a declared dependency. The delete-cache handler does re-check credential ownership before deleting.
